The study is conducted using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and the Taguchi optimization technique.
The airfoils are tested at angles of attack ranging from 0 to 15 degrees, with a 2.5-degree interval.
The RAE 2822 airfoil has the best lift-to-drag ratio among the three airfoils studied.
The coolant mass flow rate is varied from 0.01 to 0.03 kg/s, and the gas inlet temperature is varied from 60 to 180°C.
The optimum combination of coolant mass flow rate and gas inlet temperature is found to be 0.03 kg/s and 60°C, respectively.
The RAE 2822 vane is subjected to a centrifugal force of 5100 RPM to evaluate its structural stability.
The maximum stress experienced by the RAE 2822 vane under the centrifugal force is 3.996 x 10^8 N/m^2.
The maximum strain experienced by the RAE 2822 vane under the centrifugal force is 4.015 x 10^-3.
The vane material is ZAMAK, and it is coated with a 0.1 mm layer of zirconia.
The turbulence intensity considered in the study is 2%.
The study aims to optimize the gas turbine vane design for improved performance and structural stability.
The use of CFD and Taguchi optimization techniques allows for the evaluation of various design parameters and their effects on the vane's performance.
The study provides insights into the importance of impingement cooling and material selection in gas turbine vane design.
The findings of this study can be used to inform the design and development of more efficient and reliable gas turbine systems.
The paper highlights the potential of computational methods, such as CFD, in the optimization of complex engineering systems like gas turbines.
